hubs.name: ResTD
senses: A method in generative recommendation and retrieval that distills residual quantization indexing trajectories and preferences into decoder states
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method (ResTD), which utilizes residual quantization indexing trajectories to distill codeword preferences and align decoder states in generative recommendation and retrieval models.

hubs.name: Semantic ID
senses: A discrete, hierarchical representation (often produced via methods like RQ-VAE) that encodes semantic information of items or documents for generative retrieval and recommender systems.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to Semantic IDs (SIDs), which are hierarchical discrete semantic identifiers used to represent documents or items in generative retrieval and recommendation tasks.

hubs.name: RouteRec
senses: RouteRec: a behavior-guided routing and mixture-of-experts model for sequential recommendation and next-item prediction
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same sequential recommendation architecture (RouteRec), which uses behavior-guided routing to allocate experts.

hubs.name: RPTune
senses: Rank, Prune, and Finetune (RPTune), an end-to-end learned context curation framework for in-context product and catalog search using an encoder, curator, and LLM post-training
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method (RPTune / Rank, Prune, and Finetune), including its internal modules (encoder, curator), training techniques, and downstream evaluation on various LLM backbones for product catalog search.

hubs.name: Canopy
senses: A hierarchical evidence retrieval and compression framework for multimodal/long-context question answering
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method (Canopy), which uses hierarchical selection, node encoders, and evidence compression for question answering across text and multimodal benchmarks like OTT-QA, HotpotQA, and LVBench.

hubs.name: RARS
senses: Resolution-Aligned Relevance Supervision (RARS), a hierarchical generative retrieval framework and training objective for semantic identifier hierarchies.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same generative retrieval training framework/objective (RARS, or Resolution-Aligned Relevance Supervision) evaluated on tasks such as ESCI product search.

hubs.name: Effective Training Time
senses: A systems metric representing the portion or percentage of total job wall time spent on productive model training rather than overheads such as compilation, checkpointing, and failure recovery.
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently refer to Effective Training Time (ETT / ETT%), an efficiency metric measuring productive training execution time versus systems overheads.

hubs.name: Generative Retrieval
senses: An information retrieval paradigm where a model autoregressively generates document identifiers (DocIDs) in response to a query, often using constrained decoding.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same information retrieval paradigm/task known as generative retrieval, including its methods, decoding constraints, and baseline models.

hubs.name: AgentWebRec
senses: An agent-based personalized recommendation framework based on task-oriented evidence acquisition and progressive fusion over distributed agent memories
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation framework, AgentWebRec, detailing its methodology, architecture, and empirical evaluations across various benchmark datasets and baselines.

hubs.name: ESCI
senses: ESCI (Exact, Substitute, Complement, Irrelevant), also known as the Shopping Queries Dataset, is a large-scale multilingual product search benchmark dataset for e-commerce.
hubs.reason: All fragments uniformly refer to the ESCI product search benchmark dataset (Shopping Queries Dataset) across various multilingual locales.

hubs.name: MMTI
senses: A multi-grained text-to-video retrieval model featuring key feature selection and a text-video interaction module
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same text-to-video retrieval model (MMTI) evaluated on datasets like MSR-VTT and ActivityNet, incorporating multi-grained text-video interaction.

hubs.name: TemporalNarrative
senses: A recommender system profiling method that encodes recent and historical LLM-generated narrative representations using SBERT and fuses them with attention to generate candidate recommendations.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation method/strategy that leverages LLM-generated narrative representations fused via attention, evaluated across user segments and ranking metrics.

hubs.name: NDCG@10
senses: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at rank 10 (NDCG@10), a standard information retrieval and recommendation system ranking metric.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the same standard evaluation metric, NDCG cut off at position 10, used to evaluate recommendation and ranking models.

hubs.name: Jev
senses: A decision-oriented recommendation/reranking model evaluated on recommendation tasks against baselines like DCNv2 and LLM rerankers.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation/reranking model named Jev, evaluating its latency, candidate-set scalability, and NDCG@10 against LLM and recommendation baselines.

hubs.name: Narrative
senses: An LLM-generated natural-language user profile representation strategy evaluated in recommender systems
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method: a natural-language profile representation ('Narrative') generated by an LLM and encoded with Sentence-BERT for recommendation tasks.

hubs.name: SASRec
senses: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (SASRec), a sequential recommendation model that uses self-attention mechanisms over user interaction histories
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently refer to the widely known sequential recommendation model SASRec, which uses self-attention over user behavior sequences and is frequently used as a baseline.

hubs.name: SkillSeek
senses: A two-stage retriever developed for the agent skill retrieval task at scale
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same method/system, SkillSeek, which is a two-stage skill retriever for LLM agents.

hubs.name: Text-Video Retrieval
senses: A multimodal information retrieval task focused on finding relevant video content corresponding to a natural language text query (and vice versa).
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same cross-modal retrieval task (text-video / text-to-video retrieval), including its benchmarks, models, and evaluation metrics.

hubs.name: ESCI-US
senses: The English/United States locale subset of the ESCI benchmark dataset used for evaluating product retrieval and search.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the same dataset: the US English subset of the ESCI (Exact, Substitute, Complement, Irrelevant) benchmark.

hubs.name: ESCI-ES
senses: A Spanish-language partition or subset of the Amazon ESCI (Shopping Queries) benchmark dataset used for evaluating product retrieval and ranking models.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same dataset, ESCI-ES, which is the Spanish subset of the ESCI shopping queries benchmark.

hubs.name: ESCI-JP
senses: The Japanese locale/subset of the ESCI benchmark dataset used for evaluating product search and retrieval models.
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently refer to the Japanese subset (JP locale) of the ESCI product retrieval benchmark dataset.

hubs.name: OneReason
senses: A recommendation foundation model and framework that aligns semantic IDs with natural language, models multi-domain interaction histories, and leverages reasoning and reinforcement learning for recommendation tasks.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation foundation model/framework, detailing its semantic alignment, interest reasoning, multi-domain benchmarks, and training methodology.

hubs.name: LLM
senses: Large Language Model (LLM), a class of foundation AI models used for natural language processing, reasoning, generation, and extraction tasks
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the same broad concept of Large Language Models (LLMs) utilized across various downstream tasks such as summarization, attribute consolidation, and information extraction.

hubs.name: BM25
senses: A widely used probabilistic ranking function and sparse lexical information retrieval algorithm.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the classic BM25 lexical ranking/retrieval algorithm used across various information retrieval benchmarks and hybrid retrieval workflows.

hubs.name: Centroid
senses: A content-based user profiling baseline method in recommender systems that represents a user by calculating the arithmetic mean (centroid) of the embeddings of items in their interaction history.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation profiling method/baseline that computes a user representation as the average (centroid) of item embeddings across interaction history.

hubs.name: GEAR
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same end-to-end generative retrieval framework (GEAR) deployed in industrial recommendation settings (such as Douyin Ads), integrating tokenization, autoregressive generation, and reranking.

hubs.name: Neural Parser
senses: A neural network-based parser trained via distillation from a rule-based parser to extract invention graphs for downstream patent prior art search
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same specific neural parsing model evaluated against a rule-based teacher for patent invention graph generation and search.

hubs.name: Own-Model Premium
senses: A metric or parameter quantifying the degree to which an evaluator language model favors its own generated text over text produced by other models.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the identical concept: a statistical measurement or bias parameter capturing self-preference in LLM evaluators evaluating their own outputs.

hubs.name: Recommendation
senses: The core information retrieval and machine learning task of predicting user preferences and suggesting relevant candidate items based on historical interactions and behavioral context.
hubs.reason: All fragments uniformly refer to the general task and application domain of recommender systems and personalized recommendation.

hubs.name: SkillsBench
senses: An 89-task benchmark for evaluating agent skills, skill retrieval, and skill routing methods
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the same 89-task benchmark dataset used to evaluate agent skills and skill retrieval/routing methods.

hubs.name: Iterative Attribute Discovery Framework
senses: A framework designed to iteratively extract candidate attributes and values, aggregate, rank, consolidate via semantic merging, and perform cost-aware model selection from user-generated thematic corpora.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same proposed framework for discovering attributes and extracting structured data from user-generated thematic corpora such as Reddit.

hubs.name: Residual Quantization
senses: A multi-stage vector quantization technique that successively quantizes residual vectors using level-specific codebooks, often used to produce discrete hierarchical semantic IDs.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same vector quantization method (Residual Quantization/RQ) and its application to generating multi-level discrete semantic identifiers or codebooks.

hubs.name: Hierarchical Sparse Routing
senses: A multi-level mixture-of-experts routing mechanism that hierarchically scores and selects expert groups and specific experts using sparse selection.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same hierarchical sparse routing mechanism, typically deployed in recommendation models like RouteRec, which routes inputs through a hierarchy of groups and experts using sparse selection.

hubs.name: Qwen
senses: A family of open-weight large language models developed by Alibaba Cloud, utilized across diverse tasks such as candidate reranking, information extraction, and machine translation.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the Qwen family of large language models and its applications across various tasks such as pointwise/listwise candidate reranking, extraction, and translation.

hubs.name: Rule-Based Parser
senses: A hand-crafted pattern-based parser used to construct invention graphs from text and serve as a baseline and teacher label generator for a neural parser.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same rule-based baseline parser used to generate invention graphs from patent documents and serve as teacher graphs for neural model distillation.

hubs.name: Sequential Recommendation
senses: A recommendation task and paradigm that models a user's chronological interaction history as a sequence to predict subsequent user interactions
hubs.reason: All fragments consistently describe the sequential recommendation task, its purpose, and models applied to it.

hubs.name: TemporalCentroid
senses: A recommendation strategy that constructs short- and long-term item centroids from SBERT embeddings and fuses them using an attention mechanism.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same recommendation method, detailing its architecture (fusing short- and long-term centroids from SBERT embeddings using attention) and its evaluation against baseline centroid methods.

hubs.name: User Agent
senses: An LLM-based autonomous software agent representing a user to mediate platform interactions, maintain private memory/preferences, and collaborate across an agent network for personalized tasks.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the identical concept of an autonomous user-representing agent within an Agent Web framework designed for recommendation and personalized assistance.

hubs.name: Information Extraction
senses: The natural language processing task and process of automatically extracting structured information from unstructured text.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the standard NLP task of information extraction, which encompasses extracting structured data, entities, relations, and attributes from unstructured text.

hubs.name: Pass Rate
senses: An evaluation metric measuring the proportion of benchmark tasks successfully completed or solved by an autonomous agent or model.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same standard evaluation metric: pass rate (the fraction/percentage of successfully completed tasks by an agent/model).

hubs.name: Recall
senses: A standard evaluation metric representing the proportion of relevant instances that are retrieved or correctly identified.
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the standard information retrieval and machine learning metric of Recall (including Recall@K).

hubs.name: Serving-Time Gate
senses: A learned gating mechanism in recommendation systems that uses serving-time user features to selectively route users between collaborative and generative profile-driven models to balance novelty and relevance.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same specific learned routing gate method designed to balance novelty and relevance by directing users between collaborative and generative recommendation models.

hubs.name: Agent Web
senses: A decentralized, distributed network of autonomous LLM-based agents collaborating across task-conditioned pathways for information discovery and recommendations.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same concept: a decentralized network environment formed by communicating personal and platform agents (the Agent Web).

hubs.name: Books
senses: A standard benchmark dataset in recommender systems research, typically derived from Amazon book reviews (such as Amazon Books or the Books domain within benchmarks like InstructRec).
hubs.reason: All fragments refer to the Books recommendation benchmark dataset (commonly derived from Amazon reviews) used for evaluating recommender and reranking models.

hubs.name: Dense Retrieval
senses: An information retrieval paradigm that utilizes dense vector embeddings to represent queries and documents and match them via semantic similarity.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same broad information retrieval paradigm (dense retrieval) and various models or baselines operating within this framework.

hubs.name: KFS
senses: Key Feature Selection (KFS), a mechanism in video-text retrieval (specifically in MMTI) that mitigates visual redundancy by adaptively selecting informative frames and patches via multi-dimensional saliency and learnable importance scores.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the identical Key Feature Selection (KFS) mechanism designed to compact visual features and reduce redundancy in text-video retrieval within the MMTI framework.

hubs.name: Recommendation Reranking
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the task of reranking an initial candidate set of items in recommender systems based on user context and interaction history.

hubs.name: Time to Start
senses: A machine learning training performance metric (TTS) that measures the cold-start overhead and idle time incurred before productive training steps begin, functioning as a component of Effective Training Time percentage (ETT%).
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the same metric, Time to Start (TTS), which quantifies the startup and initialization overhead in machine learning training workflows as part of the ETT framework.

hubs.name: CaLIR
senses: A generative retrieval model that decodes semantic identifier (SID) tokens using an autoregressive decoder with reasoning states and auxiliary training objectives.
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the exact same model (CaLIR), a generative retrieval model that generates semantic IDs (SIDs) and is used as a baseline and foundation in several generative retrieval studies.

hubs.name: NDCG
senses: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG), a standard ranking evaluation metric measuring ranking quality at various cutoffs
hubs.reason: All fragments describe the standard information retrieval and ranking evaluation metric Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) across various cutoffs.
